title: Mind Reading 2.0: Why did you do that?

sentences.en: All parents have moments when their kids test their patience.
sentences.zh: 所有的父母都有过孩子考验他们耐心的时刻。

sentences.en: I often yell at my kids for things that they did by accident,
sentences.zh: 我经常因为孩子们无意中做的事情而对他们大喊大叫，

sentences.en: like spilling a smoothie or leaving a cap off of a permanent marker
sentences.zh: 比如洒了冰沙，或者没盖上记号笔的盖子，

sentences.en: and, you know, making black permanent stains all over the sofa.
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道的，在沙发上弄出黑色的永久性污渍。

sentences.en: When this happens and the couch is covered in black splotches
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生，沙发上布满了黑色斑点，

sentences.en: or there's smoothie on the floor,
the perpetrators inevitably offer this defense.
sentences.zh: 肇事者不可避免地会提出这样的辩解。

sentences.en: I didn't mean to do it.
I shouldn't say this, but I tell them,
sentences.zh: 我不该这么说，但我告诉他们，

sentences.en: it doesn't matter that you didn't mean to do it.
sentences.zh: 你是不是故意的并不重要。

sentences.en: What matters is that you won't do it again.
sentences.zh: 重要的是你以后不会再犯了。

sentences.en: Lian's reaction, while understandable, is deeply ironic.
sentences.zh: 莉安的反应虽然可以理解，但却非常讽刺。

sentences.en: She's a psychologist who studies how we read other people's intentions.
sentences.zh: 她是一位心理学家，专门研究我们如何解读他人的意图。

sentences.en: We need to think about other people's minds in order to figure out
sentences.zh: 我们需要思考他人的想法，以便弄清楚

sentences.en: who our friends are, who to avoid, whom to punish, whether to punish.
sentences.zh: 谁是我们的朋友，该避开谁，该惩罚谁，以及是否应该惩罚。

sentences.en: And we need to read people's intentions in any ordinary interaction,
sentences.zh: 在任何普通的互动中，我们都需要解读人们的意图，

sentences.en: like having a conversation and figuring out what to say and how to respond.
sentences.zh: 比如进行对话，弄清楚该说什么以及如何回应。

sentences.en: As we go through life, we are constantly making sense of people's actions
sentences.zh: 在我们的一生中，我们不断地通过解读他人的意图

sentences.en: Our ability to read what is happening in other people's minds
sentences.zh: 我们解读他人思想的能力

sentences.en: is like an invisible compass guiding us through life.
sentences.zh: 就像指引我们人生的隐形指南针。

sentences.en: But sometimes it leads us astray.
sentences.zh: 但有时它会把我们引入歧途。

sentences.en: We misread other people's intentions, especially when we are hurt or angry.
sentences.zh: 我们误读了他人的意图，尤其是在我们受伤或愤怒的时候。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, how our powers of observation
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》，探讨我们的观察力

sentences.en: allow us to navigate our social worlds until they don't.
sentences.zh: 如何让我们在社交世界中游刃有余，直到它们失效为止。

sentences.en: It's the start of a series we're calling Mind Reading 2.0.
sentences.zh: 这是我们称之为“读心术 2.0”系列节目的开篇。

sentences.en: It explores a topic listeners have asked us about a lot,
sentences.zh: 它探讨了一个听众经常问我们的主题，

sentences.en: how to decode what's going on in other people's heads.
sentences.zh: 即如何解读他人脑子里在想什么。

sentences.en: We are constantly trying to read other people's minds.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在试图解读他人的思想。

sentences.en: When we interact with friends, relatives, and co-workers,
sentences.zh: 当我们与朋友、亲戚和同事互动时，

sentences.en: we ask ourselves, what is going on in this other person's head?
sentences.zh: 我们会问自己，这个人的脑子里在想什么？

sentences.en: Our ability to read other minds involves an extraordinary feat of cognition.
sentences.zh: 我们解读他人思想的能力涉及一种非凡的认知壮举。

sentences.en: Yet, it mostly unfolds in our heads without us being aware of it.
sentences.zh: 然而，它大多是在我们不知不觉中在脑海中完成的。

sentences.en: Minus this skill, the simplest of interactions would be mired in confusion,
sentences.zh: 如果没有这项技能，最简单的互动也会陷入混乱

sentences.en: Leanne Young is a psychologist and neuroscientist at Boston College.
sentences.zh: 莉安·杨是波士顿学院的心理学家和神经科学家。

sentences.en: She has spent years studying this mental ability
sentences.zh: 她花了多年时间研究这种心理能力

sentences.en: and the profound effects it has on our lives.
sentences.zh: 以及它对我们生活产生的深远影响。

sentences.en: Leanne Young, welcome to Hidden Brain.
It's good to be here, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: I want to start with a very simple example that shows how important it is
sentences.zh: 我想从一个非常简单的例子开始，它展示了解读他人思想

sentences.en: for us to read what's happening in the minds of other people.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说有多么重要。

sentences.en: In the 1993 movie, Mrs. Doubtfire, starring Robin Williams,
sentences.zh: 在1993年由罗宾·威廉姆斯主演的电影《窈窕奶爸》中，

sentences.en: the characters Daniel and Miranda have split up,
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔和米兰达这两个角色分开了，

sentences.en: and Daniel comes up with this unconventional way to win Miranda back.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔想出了一个非同寻常的方法来赢回米兰达。

sentences.en: He returns to the house in disguise as Mrs. Doubtfire,
sentences.zh: 他乔装打扮成道特菲尔太太回到家中，

sentences.en: an elderly widow who seeks the role of nanny and housekeeper.
sentences.zh: 那是一位寻求担任保姆和管家职位的年长寡妇。

sentences.en: Now, he quickly wins the trust of the family.
sentences.zh: 很快，他赢得了家人的信任。

sentences.en: Very soon, Miranda is asking Mrs. Doubtfire for life advice,
sentences.zh: 没过多久，米兰达就开始向道特菲尔太太寻求生活建议，

sentences.en: including whether to go on a date with a man she's just met.
sentences.zh: 包括是否要和刚认识的男人约会。

sentences.en: Mrs. Doubtfire, may I ask you a question?
sentences.zh: 道特菲尔太太，我可以问你一个问题吗？

sentences.en: How long after Mr. Doubtfire passed away?
sentences.zh: 道特菲尔先生去世多久了？

sentences.en: Winston, did you feel any desire?
sentences.zh: 温斯顿，你还有任何欲望吗？

sentences.en: Once the father of your children is out of the picture,
sentences.zh: 一旦你孩子的父亲不在身边了，

sentences.en: the only solution is total and lifelong celibacy.
sentences.zh: 唯一的解决办法就是彻底且终身的独身。

sentences.en: So, Leanne, if we lack the capacity to read what was happening
sentences.zh: 那么，莉安，如果我们缺乏解读丹尼尔和米兰达

sentences.en: inside the minds of Daniel and Miranda,
how would that change how we understood this scene?
sentences.zh: 那会如何改变我们对这一场景的理解？

sentences.en: Well, I think we wouldn't be able to appreciate the humor and the irony
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们将无法欣赏那一幕的幽默和讽刺，

sentences.en: in that scene where Daniel is,
essentially, he knows what is going on with his wife,
sentences.zh: 本质上，他知道他妻子的情况，

sentences.en: and he is trying to get his wife to not date this other man.
sentences.zh: 他正试图阻止他妻子与那个男人约会。

sentences.en: And, of course, we know that the wife doesn't know Daniel's true identity as Daniel.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道妻子并不知道道特菲尔太太就是丹尼尔。

sentences.en: She thinks that he is this housekeeper,
and we know that she doesn't know.
sentences.zh: 而我们知道她并不知道真相。

sentences.en: And so there's this very sort of layered understanding that we need to have as the audience
sentences.zh: 所以，作为观众，我们需要具备这种非常有层次的理解，
才能觉得这一幕很有趣。

sentences.en: We can't find it funny without realizing that she doesn't know what he knows and who he is.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不意识到她不知道他所知道的事情以及他是谁，我们就不会觉得它有趣。

sentences.en: So we're able to read in some ways that he has an agenda here
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，我们能够看出他在这里有自己的目的，

sentences.en: because he wants to keep his wife from dating other men.
sentences.zh: 因为他想阻止妻子与别的男人约会。

sentences.en: And we also understand that she doesn't know what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我们也明白她并不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: But what's interesting to me, Leanne, is that we intuit all of this effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 但莉安，让我感兴趣的是，我们毫不费力地直觉到了这一切。

sentences.en: No one sits down as they're watching the movie and actually says to themselves,
sentences.zh: 没有人会在看电影时坐下来对自己说，

sentences.en: all right, this is what's going through his head,
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是他脑子里想的，

sentences.en: this is what's going through her head.
It's the fact we're able to take it in so effortlessly that allows us to understand the scene.
sentences.zh: 正是因为我们能够如此毫不费力地吸收这些信息，才让我们能够理解这一场景。

sentences.en: And I remember watching this movie as a child who, of course,
sentences.zh: 我记得小时候看这部电影时，当然，

sentences.en: hadn't had the benefit of studying how theory of mind works in the brains of children and adults.
sentences.zh: 我还没有研究过儿童和成人的心智理论是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And I still found it very funny.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然觉得它非常有趣。

sentences.en: I knew exactly what was happening, who was misunderstanding,
sentences.zh: 我完全知道发生了什么，谁误解了什么，

sentences.en: who knew what other people didn't know, and so on,
sentences.zh: 谁知道别人不知道的事情，等等，

sentences.en: in order to be able to enjoy the scene and really the entire movie.
sentences.zh: 从而能够享受这一场景，实际上是整部电影。

sentences.en: So you used the term just now, theory of mind.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才用了“心智理论”这个术语。

sentences.en: It's a term that you and other researchers have to describe our capacity
sentences.zh: 这是你和其他研究人员用来描述我们理解他人思想能力的一个术语，

sentences.en: to understand what is happening in the minds of other people.
sentences.zh: 你能为我解释一下这个术语的意思吗？

sentences.en: Can you explain what that term means to me?

sentences.zh: 我应该说，许多心理学家和神经科学家使用许多不同的术语。

sentences.en: So I should say that many psychologists and neuroscientists use a number of different terMs.
sentences.zh: 心智理论就是其中之一，

sentences.en: Theory of mind is one of those terms,
and that describes the theory that we all have,
sentences.zh: 普通人所拥有的关于他人思想的理论。

sentences.en: ordinary people have, about other people's minds.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们如何理解他人拥有思想、

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is how we understand that other people have thoughts,
sentences.zh: 信念、欲望和意图，即一般的心理状态。

sentences.en: beliefs, desires, and intentions, mental states in general.
sentences.zh: 因此，用于描述这种一般认知能力的其他术语

sentences.en: And so other terms that have been used for this general cognitive capacity
mentalizing, reasoning about intentions, and so on.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我们毫不费力地做到这一点，

sentences.en: And again, the fact that we do it so effortlessly,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们许多人甚至没有意识到我们在这样做。

sentences.en: you know, many of us don't even realize that we're doing it.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人没有意识到，如果我们正在进行对话，

sentences.en: Many of us don't realize that if we're having a conversation,
sentences.zh: 而我们无法直觉到对方脑子里在想什么，

sentences.en: and we were not able to intuit what was happening in someone else's mind,
really difficult to have a conversation.

sentences.zh: 即使在你我进行这次对话时，

sentences.en: Even as you and I are having this conversation,
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我正在努力弄清楚，你知道，

sentences.en: Shankar, I'm trying to figure out, you know,
what it is that you want to know,
sentences.zh: 以及如何以一种易于理解的方式解释“心智理论”这个术语，等等。

sentences.en: and how to explain the term theory of mind
sentences.zh: 有时我们在对话时会从人们那里获取不同的线索，

sentences.en: in a way that will be accessible, and so on.
And sometimes we take different cues from people

sentences.zh: 他们看起来是否困惑，等等。
所以我们吸收所有这些信息，
来弄清楚人们在想什么，

sentences.en: whether they look confused, and so on.
sentences.zh: 以及他们如何回应我们提供给他们的信息。

sentences.en: And so we take in all of that information
sentences.zh: 世界上几乎所有最伟大的故事

sentences.en: to figure out what people are thinking
sentences.zh: 都要求你运用心智理论，

sentences.en: and how they're responding to the information that we're giving them.
Nearly all the world's greatest stories
sentences.zh: 想想石黑一雄的《长日留痕》这样的书，

sentences.en: ask you to exercise theory of mind,
sentences.zh: 或者《绝命毒师》这样的电视剧，

sentences.en: to inhabit the minds of other people.
sentences.zh: 又或者是《汉密尔顿》这样的音乐剧。

sentences.en: Think of books such as Kazuo Ishiguro's The Remains of the Day,
sentences.zh: 我认为非常重要的一点是，当我们看电影、

sentences.en: or TV shows such as Breaking Bad,
sentences.zh: 看电视剧、读书时，我们能够站在不同角色的角度去思考。
通常，作为读者，作为观众，

sentences.en: I think it's really important that we're able to take the perspective
sentences.zh: 我们有一种不同的，在某些情况下是全知的视角。

sentences.en: of different characters when we're watching movies,
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到场景以一种场景中的角色无法看到的方式展开。
因此，在某种层面上，我们理解正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: And often, as the reader, as the viewer,
sentences.zh: 而故事中的角色却不理解，

sentences.en: we have a sort of different, in some cases, omniscient perspective.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不仅能够进入角色的思想，

sentences.en: We can see the scene unfolding in a way that characters within the scene cannot.
And so, on one level, we understand what's going on
sentences.zh: 我们能够理解正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: in a way that characters within the story do not,
sentences.zh: 而故事中的角色却不理解，

sentences.en: and we also are able to not just get into the minds of characters,
sentences.zh: 而且我们不仅能够进入角色的思想，

sentences.en: but get into the hearts of characters as well,
so we know how they're feeling and how they're reacting and responding
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能了解他们的感受，以及他们如何做出反应和回应，

sentences.en: in ways that maybe other characters in the story don't.
sentences.zh: 方式可能与故事中的其他角色不同。

sentences.en: So, psychologists have found different ways to measure this ability
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学家们找到了衡量这种能力的不同方法，

sentences.en: and to test how it develops in small children.
sentences.zh: 并测试它在幼儿身上是如何发展的。

sentences.en: Is this a skill we are born with at birth,
sentences.zh: 这是一种我们与生俱来的技能，

sentences.en: or is it something that develops over time?
sentences.zh: 还是随着时间推移而发展的？

sentences.en: This is a little bit controversial in the field,
sentences.zh: 在这个领域，这还有些争议，

sentences.en: but I think what is generally recognized in the field
sentences.zh: 但我认为该领域普遍认可的是，

sentences.en: is that at least children's capacity for explicit theory of mind,
sentences.zh: 至少儿童对外显心理理论的能力，

sentences.en: being able to reason and verbalize answers to theory of mind tasks,
sentences.zh: 即能够推理并口头回答心理理论任务的能力，

sentences.en: that ability emerges between the ages of three and five years.
sentences.zh: 这种能力在三到五岁之间出现。

sentences.en: Psychologists are able to administer batteries of theory of mind tasks
sentences.zh: 心理学家能够对幼儿进行一系列心理理论任务测试，

sentences.en: to young children to figure out when exactly it is that individual children
sentences.zh: 以准确找出个体儿童在何时

sentences.en: are able to think about other agents in the world as having minds
sentences.zh: 能够将世界上的其他主体视为拥有心理，

sentences.en: that are maybe separate from the reality of a situation.
sentences.zh: 而这些心理可能与现实情况是分离的。

sentences.en: Some of these tests create artificial situations
sentences.zh: 其中一些测试创造了人为的情境，

sentences.en: where one character knows more than another.
sentences.zh: 让一个角色比另一个角色知道得更多。

sentences.en: Daniel in Mrs. Doubtfire understands the subterfuge he is perpetrating.
sentences.zh: 《窈窕奶爸》中的丹尼尔明白他正在实施的诡计。

sentences.en: The tests evaluate whether children can keep track
sentences.zh: 这些测试评估儿童是否能追踪

sentences.en: of all the different perspectives in the minds of different characters,
sentences.zh: 不同角色心理中所有不同的视角，

sentences.en: that one person has a belief that's true, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，一个人持有真实的信念，

sentences.en: and another has a belief that's false.
sentences.zh: 而另一个人持有错误的信念。

sentences.en: So one example of a false belief task would be the Sally-Anne task
sentences.zh: 错误信念任务的一个例子是萨莉-安妮任务，

sentences.en: in which you have two puppets, Sally and Anne.
sentences.zh: 其中有两个木偶，萨莉和安妮。

sentences.en: Sally is playing with a ball, and then she takes the ball
sentences.zh: 萨莉正在玩球，然后她把球

sentences.en: and puts it away in a basket.
She leaves the room, and another puppet comes in
sentences.zh: 她离开了房间，另一个木偶进来，

sentences.en: and moves the ball to a different location,
sentences.zh: 把球移到了另一个地方，

sentences.en: and then children are asked when Sally comes back into the room,
sentences.zh: 然后问孩子们，当萨莉回到房间时，

sentences.en: where does she think her ball is?
sentences.zh: 她会认为她的球在哪里？

sentences.en: Did Sally see Anne move the block?
sentences.zh: 萨莉看到安妮移动积木了吗？
因为她当时在外面荡秋千。

sentences.en: So when Sally comes back in, where will she think the block is?
sentences.zh: 所以当萨莉回来时，她会认为积木在哪里？

sentences.en: Um, in there, but it's not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那里，但其实不在那。

sentences.en: So she'll think it's in the block.
sentences.zh: 所以她会认为它在积木里。

sentences.en: And three-year-old children will tend to say
that she thinks the ball is where it really is,
sentences.zh: 她认为球在它实际所在的地方，

sentences.en: even though she's not supposed to know that Anne came in and moved her ball,
sentences.zh: 尽管她本不应该知道安妮进来移动了她的球，

sentences.en: whereas older children, by the time children are five,
sentences.zh: 而年龄较大的孩子，到了五岁时，

sentences.en: they know that Sally has a false belief about where that ball is.
sentences.zh: 他们知道萨莉对球的位置有错误的信念。

sentences.en: So once Anne moves the ball,
sentences.zh: 所以一旦安妮移动了球，

sentences.en: small children deduce or believe that Sally must somehow intuitively also know
sentences.zh: 年幼的孩子会推断或相信萨莉一定也能直觉地知道，

sentences.en: that the ball has been moved to the new location,
sentences.zh: 球已经被移到了新位置，
而年龄较大的孩子则意识到，

sentences.en: no, Sally, in fact, does not have the same mind as Anne,
sentences.zh: 不，事实上，萨莉的心理和安妮并不一样，

sentences.en: and what Anne knows is not what Sally knows.
sentences.zh: 安妮知道的并不是萨莉知道的。

sentences.en: Sally knows only what she knows,
sentences.zh: 萨莉只知道她自己知道的，

sentences.en: and as far as she knows, the ball is in the old location.
sentences.zh: 据她所知，球还在原来的位置。

sentences.en: So when she returns to the room,
she's going to guess that that's where it still is.
Why do you think she'll think that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么认为她会那样想？
所以年幼的孩子，三岁的孩子，

sentences.en: don't have a concept that people could have beliefs in their heads
sentences.zh: 还没有一种概念，即人们脑中可能存在

sentences.en: that depart from the reality of the world,

sentences.zh: 事实情况相背离的信念。

sentences.en: So we've looked at a couple of humorous examples
sentences.zh: 我们已经看了一些幽默的例子，

sentences.en: of how theory of mind operates,
sentences.zh: 了解心理理论是如何运作的，

sentences.en: but I want to stress again this capacity we have
sentences.zh: 但我还是要再次强调我们这种能力，

sentences.en: to intuit what's happening in the minds of other people.
sentences.zh: 即直觉感知他人心理活动的能力。
